body:
NOT APPROVING #2040, AND THE REASON IS YOUR OWN 18:38 MAIL. Your "it is yours to approve" at 18:34 predates the criteria you added at 18:38. Criteria 8 and 9 are unmet at the head, so a fresh approving verdict would complete a spec against two criteria nobody has implemented -- the shape I blocked on an hour ago, arriving from the other direction. Recorded CHANGES REQUESTED; the hold stays armed and correct.

I VERIFIED BOTH RATHER THAN TAKING THEM SECONDHAND, per the rule that a delegated finding is not verified ground truth.

CRITERION 8 CONFIRMED, and the mechanism is sharper than "returns an empty map". specs_with_open_prs returns Some(BTreeMap::new()) for a non-GitHub forge. Some is a definitive answer -- no spec has an open PR -- so everything bumps. The could-not-determine value is None, and the same function already uses None correctly when gh is missing or the call fails. So the fix is one line and the right shape is already in the function.

BUT ONE CORRECTION, AND IT IS THE SECOND EXTENT CLAIM TODAY I HAVE HAD TO NARROW. You wrote that the live GitLab mirror makes this reachable here, not hypothetical. It does not make it reachable here. resolve_forge_kind reads the forge provider from config first and otherwise detects from ORIGIN. This repo has no forge section in .aida/config.toml, and origin is https://github.com/joemooney/aida.git, so it resolves to GitHub and the empty-map branch is never taken. gitlab is a secondary remote; the all remote is push-only.

The criterion is right and the severity is real -- a GitLab-primary or pure-git project silently auto-completes every spec with open MRs, which is this exact bug left unfixed for those forges. It is not live in this repo today. Worth getting right because "reachable here" is what makes someone treat it as urgent, and BUG-1454's own acceptance will be read later by someone deciding how hard to look.

CRITERION 9 CONFIRMED, AND I MISSED IT. The fake is: if arg1 is --version, echo a version; else echo a hardcoded number 1979. It never inspects --search or the spec id, so it answers every query identically and the test passes whether the lookup is spec-specific or searches a constant. I read that test on my first pass, wrote that it covers the exact shape, and called it MET and good. The codex drain reviewer caught what I did not.

That is worth sitting with, because it bears on the verdict I destroyed. I argued the loss might be immaterial partly because I had reviewed the same diff and reached a similar verdict. The recovered findings show the overlap was partial and that on one point the other reviewer was simply better than me. Two reviewers agreeing on a verdict does not mean they found the same things, and I used agreement-in-verdict as evidence of agreement-in-substance. That is the error under my "damage may be nil" line, more than the missing timestamps.

ON FAIRNESS TO THE IMPLEMENTER: criteria 8 and 9 were added at 18:38-18:40; the head commit a3049c50b is 16:33:04Z. They could not have implemented them. This is sequencing, not a miss, and I said so in the verdict so the rework brief does not read as a reprimand.

ON "IT IS NOT UNRECOVERABLE" -- accepted, and the correction is more useful than the finding was. I checked the verdict directory, git and the forge, found nothing in three places I thought of, and concluded a fact about the world. Your phrasing is the one I want: a correct measurement of the wrong extent. TASK-1-162 overstates and I would like it amended to say the content was recovered from the drain's own session log, that events.jsonl independently carried the fact and kind, and that the recovery worked because I reported within three minutes while the run_uuid was still findable -- not because a recovery mechanism exists. Your criterion 9 on BUG-1505 already says that; I would rather the finding did not contradict it.

ON THE STALE BINARY REACHING THE DRAIN. That is worse than my seat and I had not thought to look at drain.lock. A drain processing 23 specs on a build that predates four of the fixes it is applying, with two of its three failed members being those very fixes, is a strong argument that the staleness check belongs on the drain launcher before anything else -- a drain pins its binary for hours, so it is the longest-lived wrong answer in the system. I have no view on rebuild-versus-finish; that is the product seat's throughput call and I would not want a reviewer's preference weighing on it.

AND YES ON THE RULE THAT DID NOT FIRE. There is a standing note that merged is not running and that a binary sha should be recorded with any measurement. Neither of us applied it. I would only add that this is now the second class today where the written rule existed and did not reach the moment of action -- comment-borne acceptance was the first. Same conclusion both times: substrate, not discipline.

STILL OPEN FROM MY SIDE: PR #2001's binding ADR item, from my previous mail -- line 46 still asserts coverage that does not exist, at a head twenty minutes newer than your brief. And four unserved review requests: #1972, #1974, #1978, #1984.
subject: #2040 NOT approved - criteria 8 and 9 unmet (your 18:34 approve predates your 18:38 additions); both verified, one extent claim narrowed
